facts.text: The study annealed 1 µm-spaced Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 nanoribbon arrays at 700 K in flowing Ar containing 2% N2, using a 10 K/min heating rate.
Continuous Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 films on Kapton were subjected to cyclic longitudinal tensile strain over 0–1% and 0–2% ranges.
The study compared lithographically patterned nanoribbon arrays having 1 µm versus 2 µm inter-ribbon spacing.
Magnetic measurements were performed from 2 to 300 K under 1 kOe in ZFC and FC modes, with the field oriented parallel or perpendicular to the ribbon axis.
Magnetocaloric entropy changes were derived by the Maxwell relation from magnetization isotherms measured between 5 and 200 K in fields up to 50 kOe.

Annealing at 700 K caused short-range atomic reordering and relieved fabrication-induced internal strain while leaving the amorphous matrix without detectable bulk recrystallization or phase decomposition.
The annealing-induced structural relaxation reduced local domain-pinning barriers and improved collective ferromagnetic alignment, increasing the effective ferromagnetic volume fraction.
A 2 µm ribbon separation suppressed inter-ribbon magnetic coupling, producing magnetically decoupled ribbons.
Relative to the as-deposited 1 µm-spaced arrays, 700 K annealing increased both magnetization and the maximum conventional isothermal magnetic entropy change without bulk crystallization.
Annealing increased the 5 K maximum magnetization from approximately 48–50 emu/g to 74–75 emu/g.
At 140 K and a 50 kOe field change, annealing increased the maximum −ΔSM from about 1.25 to 1.35 J kg−1 K−1.
Elastic longitudinal strain up to 2% enhanced magnetization above 100 K while leaving the approximately 70 K blocking peak and film in-plane isotropy essentially unchanged.
